hints: Focus on what an ammonium ion needs to turn into ammonia gas, think about acids versus bases.
Mixtures 1 and 2 both supply free hydroxide ions from NaOH and Ba(OH)2, so check what $\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$ always makes.
Remember that $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ forms hydroxide in water while HCl is an acid, so decide which of 3 and 4 can still supply $\text{OH}^-$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the key test for ammonium ions**

Ammonium salts release ammonia when warmed with a base. The hydroxide ion removes a proton from ammonium.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check mixtures 1 and 2**

Both NaOH and $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ are strong soluble bases. They provide plenty of $\text{OH}^-$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check mixture 3, the hidden base**

$\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is a basic oxide. In aqueous solution it reacts with water to make NaOH, so it also provides $\text{OH}^-$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$

**Check mixture 4, the acid case**

HCl is an acid, not a base. It cannot remove a proton from $\text{NH}_4^+$, it just forms another ammonium salt and phosphoric acid. No $\text{NH}_3$ is liberated.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$(\text{NH}_4)_3\text{PO}_4 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow 3\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

options.A: Correct. 1, 2 and 3 all provide base. 1 and 2 provide $\text{OH}^-$ directly, and 3 provides $\text{OH}^-$ indirectly via $\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Mixture 4 with HCl cannot produce ammonia.
options.B: Incorrect. This correctly includes 1 and 2 but wrongly leaves out 3. The trap is thinking $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is not a base, but in water it forms NaOH and so does release $\text{NH}_3$.
options.C: Incorrect. This wrongly leaves out 1. Mixture 1 is the classic $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ plus NaOH reaction used to test for ammonium, and it definitely gives $\text{NH}_3$.
options.D: Incorrect. Mixture 4 does not give ammonia because HCl is an acid. Ammonium ions stay as $\text{NH}_4^+$ in acid, they only release $\text{NH}_3$ with base.
